chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja'far ibn Uthman, from Sama'a, from Abu Basir and Wuhayb ibn Hafs, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily for God there are two (types of) knowledge — a knowledge concealed and treasured, none knows it except Him, and from that comes al-Bada'; and a knowledge He taught to His angels, His Messengers, and His Prophets — and we know it.

key_terms.الْبَدَاءُ: al-Bada' — the theological concept of God's 'alteration' of a prior divine decree; a key Shia doctrine distinguishing between what God has revealed and what He withholds
key_terms.عَلَّمَهُ مَلَائِكَتَهُ: Knowledge taught to His angels — the second category: revealed knowledge shared with celestial and prophetic recipients
key_terms.عِلْمٌ مَكْنُونٌ مَخْزُونٌ: Concealed and treasured knowledge — God's absolute, unrevealed knowledge from which al-Bada' originates

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq teach about al-Bada' and the two types of divine knowledge in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates the Shia theological doctrine of al-Bada' — the concept that God possesses a hidden, absolute knowledge from which He exercises His will to alter decrees, distinct from the knowledge He has communicated to angels, prophets, and Imams. This hadith teaches that the Imams share in the revealed category of divine knowledge, thus affirming both divine transcendence and the Imam's unique epistemic station. The doctrine of al-Bada' was controversial in early Islamic theology and this narration explains its metaphysical basis: God's inscrutable knowledge contains possibilities that He manifests in history as He wills.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ja’far Bin Usman, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer, and Wuheyb Bin Hafs, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘For Allah<sup>azwj</sup> there are two (types of) Knowledge – a Knowledge Concealed, Treasured, none know it except for Him<sup>azwj</sup>. From that is the occurrence of the Changing of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’s Decision; and a Knowledge Taught to His<sup>azwj</sup> Angels and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasools<sup>as</sup>, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophets. So we<sup>asws</sup> know it’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn sa‘id from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abdallah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“Nothing appeared to Allah in a thing except that He knew it before al-Bada’ would take place.”
